### LOW: Installer now persists the serving coordinator URL into provider\.toml, so a Host\-derived installer URL becomes a lasting provider redirect
[coordinator/api/install\.sh:28](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/813c561a173c6e2aa3d075439d37b3309bb64d01/coordinator/api/install.sh#L28) · A-008, ADV-003, T-040, TB-002

The new bind\_provider\_coordinator writes \`\[coordinator\] url = wss://<host>/ws/provider\` into \~/\.config/darkbloom/provider\.toml whenever COORD\_URL is not exactly https://api\.darkbloom\.dev\. COORD\_URL comes from the coordinator's serve\-time substitution, which falls back to the request Host/X\-Forwarded\-Proto when baseURL is unset \(T\-040\)\. Previously a spoofed or poisoned installer URL only affected that one install run, because the bundle signature is pinned to the Developer ID requirement\. Now a poisoned installer \(cached, or served by a mis\-configured coordinator\) permanently points the provider at an attacker\-controlled https host\. That host would then receive the provider's registration, attestation blobs, challenge traffic and any login/provider\-token flow on later \`darkbloom start\`/\`login\`/update runs\. provider\_websocket\_url only checks the host regex and the http\-localhost rule; it does not check an allowlist of Darkbloom domains\. A user who ran the installer with a custom COORD\_URL also has their existing \`\[coordinator\] url\` silently removed when installing from production, without confirmation\. Fix: require baseURL to be configured before the coordinator serves an installer that binds a URL, or pin an allowlist of known Darkbloom coordinator hosts, and prompt or warn before overwriting an existing url\. Update the threat model for T\-040/TB\-002 to cover persisted coordinator binding\.
